      ],
      "description": "The ID of the child mail folder containing the message. This must be a base64-encoded folder ID (e.g., 'AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS. Well-known names are NOT valid for child folders."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for getting a specific message from a child mail folder."

## OUTLOOK_GET_CHILD_FOLDER_MESSAGE_CONTENT
Tool to get the MIME content of a message from a child mail folder. Use when you need to download the raw MIME format of an email message for analysis or archival.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetChildFolderMessageContentRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id",
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com",
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f"
      ],
      "description": "User's email address, UPN, or 'me' for the currently authenticated user. Use 'me' for delegated authentication or provide a specific user ID/email for S2S (app-only) authentication."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZKAAAAMZNiu9q3Y9Ioi7whL2EyrIAAABTSdTnAAAA",
        "AAMkAGI2TCCC="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the message whose MIME content to retrieve. Must be obtained from message listing or query operations."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQwAAAA=",
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the parent mail folder. Must be obtained from 'List Mail Folders' or other mail folder operations."
    },
    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZKAAAAA==",
        "AAMkAGI2TBBB="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the child mail folder within the parent folder. Must be obtained from 'List Child Mail Folders' or other folder operations."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for getting a message's MIME content from a child folder."
}

## OUTLOOK_GET_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDER
Tool to retrieve a specific child mail folder from a parent mail folder. Use when you need details about a specific subfolder within a folder hierarchy.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetChildMailFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        "id,displayName,childFolderCount",
        "id,displayName,totalItemCount,unreadItemCount"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of mailFolder properties to include in the response. Valid properties include: id, displayName, parentFolderId, childFolderCount, unreadItemCount, totalItemCount, sizeInBytes, isHidden. Example: 'id,displayName,childFolderCount'."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com",
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "sentitems",
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQwAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the parent mail folder. Common well-known names include: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. For folder IDs, obtain them from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or previous childFolders responses. Folder IDs are base64-encoded strings (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') that are mailbox-specific and must come from the same user's mailbox."
    },
    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZJwAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique ID of the child folder to retrieve. Obtain child folder IDs from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS or previous API responses. Child folder IDs are base64-encoded strings that are mailbox-specific and must come from the same user's mailbox."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for retrieving a specific child mail folder."
}

## OUTLOOK_GET_EVENT
Retrieves the full details of a specific calendar event by its ID from a user's Outlook calendar, provided the event exists.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetEventRequest",
  "required": [
    "event_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user's primary SMTP address, user principal name (UPN), or the alias 'me' (for the signed-in user) to identify the calendar owner.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the calendar owner whose events you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own calendar."
    },
    "event_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Event Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TG9tYVyGdUHg=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar event to retrieve.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Event ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique ID of the calendar event you want to retrieve. You can copy this from a previous event list or search result."
    }
  }
}

        },

        },

## OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_DELTA
Retrieve incremental changes (delta) of messages in a mailbox. FIRST RUN: Returns ALL messages in folder (use top=50 to limit). Response has @odata.deltaLink. SUBSEQUENT: Pass stored deltaLink to get only NEW/UPDATED/DELETED messages since last sync. Properties available: id, subject, from, receivedDateTime, isRead, etc. NOT available: internetMessageHeaders, full body, attachment content (response size limits).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMailDeltaRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",

        100
      ],

          "hasAttachments",
          "importance"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of message properties to include (e.g. ['subject','receivedDateTime']). Delta sync has property limitations due to response size constraints. Not available in delta: internetMessageHeaders, body (full), attachments (full content). Available: id, subject, from, toRecipients, ccRecipients, bccRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, isRead, isDraft, importance, hasAttachments, categories, conversationId, flag, webLink, bodyPreview (first 255 chars).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Select Properties",

For custom folders, use the folder ID GUID from LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS. Defaults to 'inbox' when omitted.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Folder ID",

      "human_parameter_name": "Skip Token",

## OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_FOLDER
Tool to retrieve a mail folder by ID or well-known name. Use when you need to get details about a specific folder such as item counts, size, and folder properties.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMailFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        "id,displayName,totalItemCount",
        "id,displayName,unreadItemCount"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. Valid properties: id, displayName, parentFolderId, childFolderCount, unreadItemCount, totalItemCount, sizeInBytes, isHidden."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGVmMDEzMTM4AAA=",
        "sentitems",
        "drafts"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the mail folder to retrieve. ONLY these specific well-known names are valid as string names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. Arbitrary folder names (e.g., 'workjournal') are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for retrieving a mail folder by ID or well-known name."
}

## OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGE
Tool to retrieve a specific message from a mail folder by its ID. Use when you need to fetch full message details including subject, body, sender, recipients, timestamps, and other metadata from a specific mail folder.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMailFolderMessageRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "from",
          "receivedDateTime"
        ],
        [
          "subject",
          "body",
          "from",
          "toRecipients"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of message properties to include in the response. Valid properties include: id, subject, from, toRecipients, ccRecipients, bccRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, body, bodyPreview, categories, conversationId, flag, internetMessageHeaders, parentFolderId, replyTo, sender, webLink, isDraft, isReadReceiptRequested, isDeliveryReceiptRequested, changeKey, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, inferenceClassification. Leave empty to return all fields."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA=",
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQwAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAARTQwgAAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique ID of the message to retrieve. Accepts message IDs from: OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES (message.id), OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS (message.id), OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGES (message.id), or OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES (use hitId from search results). The message must exist in the specified mail folder; otherwise, a 404 error will occur."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=",
        "sentitems"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the mail folder containing the message. ONLY these specific well-known names are valid as string names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. Arbitrary folder names (e.g., 'workjournal') are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for retrieving a specific message from a mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGE_RULE
Tool to retrieve a specific message rule from a user's mail folder. Use when you need details about an email rule in a particular user's folder.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMailFolderMessageRuleRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "mail_folder_id",
    "rule_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "rule_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Rule Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQAAAE-SSTc=",
        "AQAAAFNJXiU="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the message rule to retrieve. This can be obtained from list email rules actions."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com",
        "6640adbb5cb743b0"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the user. Can be the user's email address, user principal name (UPN), or user ID. Use 'me' for the authenticated user."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQwAAAA=",
        "drafts"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the mail folder containing the message rule. Well-known names include: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive'. For other folders, use the folder ID obtained from list mail folders actions."
    }
  }
}
```

## OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_TIPS
Tool to retrieve mail tips such as automatic replies and mailbox full status. Use when you need to check recipient status before sending mail.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMailTipsRequest",
  "required": [
    "EmailAddresses",
    "MailTipsOptions"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User principal name (UPN) or 'me' for the signed-in user.",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to use for this request. Use 'me' to use your own mailbox."
    },
    "EmailAddresses": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string",
        "format": "email"
      },
      "title": "Email Addresses",
      "examples": [
        [
          "danas@contoso.com",
          "fannyd@contoso.com"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Collection of SMTP addresses of recipients to get MailTips for.",
      "human_parameter_description": "Email addresses of the people you plan to email. This helps check things like out-of-office replies or mailbox limits before you send."
    },
    "MailTipsOptions": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "enum": [
          "automaticReplies",
          "customMailTip",
          "deliveryRestriction",
          "externalMemberCount",
          "mailboxFullStatus",
          "maxMessageSize",
          "moderationStatus",
          "recipientScope",
          "recipientSuggestions",
          "totalMemberCount"
        ],
        "type": "string",
        "title": "MailTipsOption"
      },
      "title": "Mail Tips Options",
      "examples": [
        [
          "automaticReplies",
          "mailboxFullStatus"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of mail tip types to retrieve for each recipient.",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select the types of tips you want to see for each recipient, such as automatic replies or mailbox full status."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request model to retrieve MailTips for specified recipients."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_GET_MASTER_CATEGORIES
Tool to retrieve the user's master category list. Use when you need to get all categories defined for the user.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMasterCategoriesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        5,
        10
      ],

      "human_parameter_description": "How many categories to return at most in this request. Use this to limit the list if you only need the first few results."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        5
      ],
      "description": "Number of master categories to skip for pagination (OData $skip).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Skip Count",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many categories to skip from the start of the list. Use this to move to the next page of results."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "color eq 'preset0'"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query to filter master categories.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Filter Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "A simple filter to narrow the list, such as by color or name. If you know a condition (e.g., color equals 'preset0'), enter it here to show only matching categories."

    "select": {

      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",

          "id",
          "displayName",
          "color"

      },
      "title": "Orderby",

        ]
      ],
      "description": "OData $orderby query to order master categories by property values.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Order By",

      "default": "me",
      "examples": [

      "description": "The user's unique identifier or principal name. Use 'me' for the signed-in user.",

        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f"

      ],
      "description": "The ID of the child folder containing the contact. For deeply nested folders, provide only the immediate parent folder ID."

      ],

  },

}

## OUTLOOK_GET_ME_CONTACT_PHOTO
Tool to get the binary media content of a contact's profile photo. Use when you need to download or retrieve a contact's picture.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetMeContactPhotoRequest",
  "required": [
    "contact_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID or email address. Required for app-only (S2S) authentication. If not provided, uses '/me' endpoint for delegated auth."
    },
    "contact_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Contact Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGViNGRjYTkEtcAAA=",
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQ4AAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0nIuwAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the contact whose photo to retrieve. Must be obtained from 'List Contacts' or 'Get Contact'."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for getting a contact's photo binary data."
}

## OUTLOOK_GET_ME_CONTACTS
Retrieves a specific Outlook contact by its `contact_id` from the contacts of a specified `user_id` (defaults to 'me' for the authenticated user).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetContactRequest",
  "required": [
    "contact_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's principal name (e.g., 'AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com') or 'me' for the authenticated user. Using 'me' is recommended for accessing one's own contacts.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose contacts you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own contacts."
    },
    "contact_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Contact Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "Unique identifier for the contact within the specified user's Outlook address book.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Contact ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of the contact you want to view. You can get this from a previous contact list or search."
    }
  }
}

```json

      "title": "Expand",
      "examples": [

      "type": "string",

Arbitrary folder names (e.g., 'workjournal') are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."

## OUTLOOK_GET_SCHEDULE
Retrieves free/busy schedule information for specified email addresses within a defined time window. Read-only; does not reserve time or prevent conflicts — verify availability before creating events.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetScheduleRequest",
  "required": [
    "schedules",
    "startTime",
    "endTime"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "endTime": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "End Time",
      "required": [
        "dateTime",
        "timeZone"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "dateTime": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Date Time",
          "examples": [
            "2024-07-15T09:00:00",
            "2024-12-25T18:30:00"
          ],
          "description": "A single point in time, expressed in a combined date and time format (ISO 8601). Example: '2023-10-26T10:00:00'."
        },
        "timeZone": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Time Zone",
          "examples": [
            "UTC",
            "Eastern Standard Time",
            "Pacific Standard Time"
          ],
          "description": "The time zone for the 'dateTime'. Uses standard time zone names. Example: 'Pacific Standard Time'."
        }
      },
      "description": "The end date, time, and time zone for the period for which to retrieve schedules. The period can be up to 62 days. Object must include `dateTime` (ISO 8601) and `timeZone` (valid Windows or IANA identifier). Must use same timezone convention as `startTime`.",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "human_parameter_name": "End Time",
      "human_parameter_description": "When your availability search should end. Pick the date, time, and time zone to stop looking (up to 62 days from the start)."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@domain.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID or principal name of the user whose calendar to query. Required for S2S (application) authentication. Can be either the GUID user ID (e.g., '43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f') or the user principal name (e.g., 'user@domain.com'). If not provided, the endpoint will use '/me' which requires delegated authentication.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",

        ],
        [

        ]
      ],
      "description": "A list of SMTP email addresses for users, distribution lists, or resources whose schedules are to be retrieved. Maximum of 20 addresses. Include all relevant participants; omitted addresses may cause slots to appear falsely free. External or invalid addresses may silently return no data.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Email Addresses",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email addresses of the people or rooms you want to check for availability. Add one or more addresses to see when they're free or busy."

      "description": "The start date, time, and time zone for the period for which to retrieve schedules. Object must include `dateTime` (ISO 8601) and `timeZone` (valid Windows or IANA identifier, e.g., 'UTC', 'Eastern Standard Time'). Invalid or naive timezone values cause HTTP 400 or silent DST-shifted windows.",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "human_parameter_name": "Start Time",

## OUTLOOK_GET_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES
Tool to retrieve supported languages in the user's mailbox. Use when you need to display or select from available mailbox languages.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetSupportedLanguagesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",

## OUTLOOK_GET_USER_CALENDAR_GROUP_CALENDAR_PERMISSION
Tool to retrieve a specific calendar permission for a user's calendar within a calendar group. Use when you need to check access permissions for a specific calendar.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetUserCalendarGroupCalendarPermissionRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "calendar_group_id",
    "calendar_id",
    "permission_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "6640adbb5cb743b0",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the user. Cannot use 'me' shortcut - must be actual user ID or userPrincipalName."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHO0AAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar within the calendar group."
    },
    "permission_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Permission Id",
      "examples": [
        "YTM2ZWYxZjUtY2RjZS00NjNhLWFmNDAtZmIyOGRiYjg5ZTNl"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar permission to retrieve."
    },
    "calendar_group_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Group Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHOwAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar group."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request to get a specific calendar permission from a user's calendar within a calendar group."
}

## OUTLOOK_GET_USER_CALENDAR_GROUP_EVENT_ATTACHMENT
Tool to retrieve a specific attachment from an event within a calendar group for a user. Use when you need to access attachment content from a calendar event in a user's calendar group.

**Input schema:**
```json

  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetUserCalendarGroupEventAttachmentRequest",
  "required": [
    "calendar_group_id",
    "calendar_id",
    "event_id",
    "attachment_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com",
        "6640adbb5cb743b0"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the user. Can use 'me' as shortcut for authenticated user."
    },
    "event_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Event Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQ0AAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mNQAAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the event."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [

      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar within the calendar group."
    },
    "attachment_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Attachment Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQ0AAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mNQAAAAAESABAAvczcJ9W1pkmGXYR-RDdQUQ=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the attachment to retrieve."
    },
    "calendar_group_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Group Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHOwAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar group."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for retrieving a specific attachment from an event in a calendar group for a user."
}

## OUTLOOK_GET_USER_CHILD_FOLDER_MESSAGE
Tool to retrieve a specific message from a child folder within a user's mail folder hierarchy. Use when you need to access messages from nested folders where both parent and child folder IDs are known.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetUserChildFolderMessageRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "mail_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id",
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "from",
          "receivedDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of message properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties include: id, subject, from, toRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, body, bodyPreview, categories, conversationId, internetMessageHeaders. Leave empty to return all fields."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "6640adbb5cb743b0",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the user. Must be an actual user ID (e.g., '6640adbb5cb743b0') or user principal name (UPN). Cannot use 'me' alias for this endpoint."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZKAAAAMZNiu9q3Y9Ioi7whL2EyrIAAABTSdTiAAAA"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the message to retrieve from the child folder. Must be a valid message ID obtained from list or search operations."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQwAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the parent mail folder. Must be a base64-encoded folder ID (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or similar endpoints."
    },
    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZKAAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the child folder within the parent mail folder. Must be a base64-encoded folder ID obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS or similar endpoints."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for retrieving a specific message from a child folder within a mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_GET_USER_MESSAGES_ATTACHMENTS
Tool to retrieve a specific attachment from a message in a mail folder hierarchy. Use when you need to get attachment details including content from a specific folder path.

**Input schema:**

{

        "user@example.com",

      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the email message. Obtain from OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES, OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS, or OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES."
    },
    "attachment_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Attachment Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZKAAAAMZNiu9q3Y9Ioi7whL2EyrIAAABTSdTiAAAAARIAEABETXCWuSK5RrSkPv7n2PdC"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the attachment. Obtain from LIST_OUTLOOK_ATTACHMENTS action (use the 'id' field, NOT the 'name' field)."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQwAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the parent mail folder. Can be a well-known folder name ('inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', etc.) or a folder ID (base64-encoded string obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS)."

    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZKAAAAA=="

If omitted, targets the message directly inside mailFolders/{id}. Must be a base64-encoded folder ID obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for getting a specific attachment from a message in a mail folder hierarchy."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CALENDAR_GROUP_CALENDAR_EVENTS
Tool to list events from a specific calendar within a calendar group for a user. Use when you need to retrieve events from a user's calendar that belongs to a specific calendar group.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListCalendarGroupCalendarEventsRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "calendar_group_id",
    "calendar_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of events to retrieve per page for pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of initial events to bypass, used for pagination."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "start/dateTime ge '2024-07-01T00:00:00Z'",
        "start/dateTime ge '2024-07-01T00:00:00Z' and start/dateTime le '2024-07-31T23:59:59Z'",
        "contains(subject, 'Project Review') and categories/any(c:c eq 'Work')"
      ],
      "description": "OData query string to filter calendar events. ONLY the following properties support filtering: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'subject', 'categories', 'importance', 'sensitivity', 'isAllDay', 'isCancelled', 'isReminderOn', 'type'. CRITICAL: Properties like 'body', 'bodyPreview', 'location', 'locations', 'organizer', 'attendees' do NOT support $filter and will cause errors. IMPORTANT: Use calendar event properties ONLY. Do NOT use mail/message properties like 'receivedDateTime'. For start/end filtering, you MUST use 'start/dateTime' and 'end/dateTime' ONLY. DO NOT use 'start/date' or 'end/date' - these properties do NOT exist and will cause errors. DateTime format: \"start/dateTime ge 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'\" (requires single quotes and timezone suffix). Operators: ge (>=), le (<=), eq (=), gt (>), lt (<). DateTime values without quotes or timezone suffix will be automatically normalized."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "subject",
          "start",
          "end",
          "location"
        ],
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "organizer",
          "webLink"
        ],
        [
          "body"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of specific event property names to return. MUST be provided as a list. If omitted, a default set of properties is returned. Valid field names: id, subject, body, bodyPreview, start, end, isAllDay, organizer, attendees, location, locations, recurrence, importance, sensitivity, showAs, categories, hasAttachments, webLink, onlineMeeting, onlineMeetingProvider, onlineMeetingUrl, isOnlineMeeting, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, changeKey, iCalUId, type, seriesMasterId, isOrganizer, isReminderOn, reminderMinutesBeforeStart, responseRequested, responseStatus, allowNewTimeProposals, hideAttendees, isCancelled, isDraft, originalStart, originalStartTimeZone, originalEndTimeZone, transactionId, cancelledOccurrences. Note: 'creator' is NOT a valid field - use 'organizer' instead. Invalid field names will be automatically filtered out."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        [
          "start/dateTime desc"
        ],
        [
          "subject asc",
          "importance desc"
        ],
        [
          "lastModifiedDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of properties to sort results by. Each item is a string like 'start/dateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. MUST be provided as a list, even for single sort criteria. Use 'asc' (default) or 'desc' for order. IMPORTANT: Use calendar event properties ONLY. Do NOT use mail/message properties like 'receivedDateTime'. Valid sortable datetime fields: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'createdDateTime', 'lastModifiedDateTime'."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "user@example.com",
        "AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com",
        "6640adbb5cb743b0"
      ],
      "description": "The user's primary SMTP address, user principal name (UPN), or user ID to identify the calendar owner."
    },
    "timezone": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Timezone",
      "default": "UTC",
      "examples": [
        "America/New_York",
        "Eastern Standard Time",
        "UTC",
        "Europe/London"
      ],
      "description": "Preferred timezone for event start/end times. Accepts IANA format (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Tokyo') or Windows format (e.g., 'Eastern Standard Time', 'Pacific Standard Time'). Falls back to 'UTC' if the timezone cannot be resolved."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHO0AAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar within the calendar group."
    },
    "calendar_group_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Group Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHOwAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar group containing the calendar."
    }
  }
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CALENDAR_GROUP_CALENDARS
Tool to retrieve calendars belonging to a specific calendar group. Use when you need to list calendars within a calendar group with optional OData queries.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListCalendarGroupCalendarsRequest",
  "required": [
    "calendar_group_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        5,
        10
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of calendars to return (OData $top)."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        5
      ],
      "description": "Number of calendars to skip (OData $skip)."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CALENDAR_GROUP_EVENT_ATTACHMENTS
Tool to list attachments for a calendar event within a specific calendar group for a user. Use when you need to retrieve attachments from an event in a calendar that belongs to a calendar group for a specific user.

**Input schema:**

    "calendar_id",

      ],

      "items": {
        "type": "string"

          "contentType"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of attachment properties to include (OData $select)."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },

        ]
      ],
      "description": "Order by clauses to sort the results (OData $orderby)."
    },

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CALENDAR_VIEW_DELTA
Tool to get calendar events that have been added, deleted, or updated in a calendar view. Use when you need to track changes to events within a specific time range.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListCalendarViewDeltaRequest",
  "required": [
    "start_datetime",
    "end_datetime"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "KaranVaidya@authkit.ai"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID (GUID format like '43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f') or user principal name (email format like 'user@domain.com') of the mailbox to access. Required for app-only (S2S) authentication with application permissions. If not provided, uses '/me' endpoint which requires delegated permissions."
    },
    "skiptoken": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Skiptoken",
      "examples": [
        "RPT_CxkRnN...",
        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/calendarView/delta?..."
      ],
      "description": "A state token returned in the @odata.nextLink URL of the previous delta function call. Accepts either the full @odata.nextLink URL or just the bare token value. Use this to page through large result sets during initial sync or updates. Keep paginating until you receive '@odata.deltaLink' instead of nextLink."
    },
    "deltatoken": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Deltatoken",
      "examples": [
        "OD9T9Jfo3XDIK7lG2PsqM...",
        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/calendarView/delta?..."
      ],
      "description": "A state token returned in the @odata.deltaLink URL of the previous delta function call. Accepts either the full @odata.deltaLink URL or just the bare token value. Use this to get only changes since the last sync. On first call, omit this parameter to get all events in the time range. Store the @odata.deltaLink from the response for subsequent calls."
    },
    "end_datetime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "End Datetime",
      "examples": [
        "2025-03-13T23:59:59.9999999",
        "2025-03-13T23:59:59Z"
      ],
      "description": "The end date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format. For example, '2015-11-08T20:00:00.0000000' or '2015-11-08T20:00:00Z'. This parameter is required for the first delta query to establish the time window."
    },
    "start_datetime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Start Datetime",
      "examples": [
        "2025-02-11T00:00:00.0000000",
        "2025-02-11T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "description": "The start date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format. For example, '2015-11-08T19:00:00.0000000' or '2015-11-08T19:00:00Z'. This parameter is required for the first delta query to establish the time window."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for retrieving delta changes in a calendar view."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CHAT_MESSAGES
Tool to list messages in a Teams chat. Use when you need message IDs to select a specific message for further actions.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListChatMessagesRequest",
  "required": [
    "chat_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "maximum": 50,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of messages per page (max 50)."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "createdDateTime gt 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "description": "OData filter expression for date/time filtering; honored when matching orderby property."
    },
    "chat_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Chat Id",
      "description": "ID of the chat to retrieve messages from."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        "lastModifiedDateTime desc"
      ],
      "description": "Order by property; supports 'lastModifiedDateTime desc' or 'createdDateTime desc'."
    },
    "skiptoken": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Skiptoken",
      "description": "Pagination token from the @odata.nextLink of a previous response. Pass the $skiptoken value (not the full URL) to retrieve the next page of results."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing messages in a Teams chat."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CHATS
Tool to list Teams chats. Use when you need chat IDs and topics to select a chat for further actions.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListChatsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "maximum": 50,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10
      ],
      "description": "Number of chat items per page (max 50)."
    },
    "expand": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Expand",
      "examples": [
        "members"
      ],
      "description": "Related entities to expand: 'members' or 'lastMessagePreview'."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "startswith(topic,'Project')"
      ],
      "description": "OData filter expression to filter chats, such as by topic."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        "lastMessagePreview/createdDateTime desc"
      ],
      "description": "Properties to order by; only 'lastMessagePreview/createdDateTime desc' is supported (ascending order not supported)."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User ID (GUID or email) to list chats for. Required for S2S (app-only) authentication. If not provided, uses '/me' endpoint (requires delegated authentication)."
    },
    "skiptoken": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Skiptoken",
      "description": "Pagination token from the @odata.nextLink of a previous response. Pass the $skiptoken value (not the full URL) to retrieve the next page of results."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing Teams chats."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_FOLDER_CONTACTS
Tool to retrieve contacts from a user's child contact folder. Use when you need to access contacts organized in nested folder structures for a specific user.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListChildFolderContactsRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "contact_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        25,
        50
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of contacts to retrieve per page (1-999)."
    },
    "skip": {

      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of contacts to skip from the beginning of the result set, for pagination. Use with 'top' to iterate through large contact lists."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "startsWith(displayName,'B')",
        "givenName eq 'John' and surname eq 'Doe'"
      ],
      "description": "OData V4 filter expression for targeted retrieval."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },

      "examples": [

        ],
        [
          "givenName",
          "surname",
          "companyName",
          "jobTitle"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of specific contact properties to retrieve. Valid Contact properties: displayName, givenName, surname, middleName, nickName, title, generation, emailAddresses, imAddresses, jobTitle, companyName, department, officeLocation, profession, businessHomePage, assistantName, manager, homePhones, mobilePhone, businessPhones, spouseName, personalNotes, children, homeAddress, businessAddress, otherAddress, categories, birthday, fileAs, initials, yomiGivenName, yomiSurname, yomiCompanyName, parentFolderId, changeKey, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime."
    },

      },

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_FOLDER_MESSAGES
Tool to list messages from a child folder within a parent mail folder. Use when you need to retrieve messages from a subfolder that exists within another folder.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListChildFolderMessagesRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of messages to return per request (1-1000). Always check response['@odata.nextLink'] for pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of messages to skip from the beginning of the result set, for pagination."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "isRead eq false",
        "from/emailAddress/address eq 'sender@example.com'",
        "receivedDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query to filter messages. Examples: 'isRead eq false', 'from/emailAddress/address eq 'sender@example.com'', 'receivedDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'hasAttachments eq true'. Note: Combining complex filters (especially on nested properties like 'from/emailAddress/address') with the 'orderby' parameter may fail with an InefficientFilter error. In such cases, remove 'orderby' or apply sorting client-side."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "from",
          "receivedDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of message properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties include: id, subject, from, toRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, body, bodyPreview, categories, conversationId."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        "receivedDateTime desc",
        "subject asc"
      ],
      "description": "Property to sort results by with direction. OData $orderby parameter. Example: 'receivedDateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. Note: Using 'orderby' together with complex 'filter' queries (especially on nested properties like 'from/emailAddress/address') may fail with an InefficientFilter error. If this occurs, either remove 'orderby' or apply sorting client-side."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=",
        "sentitems"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the parent mail folder. ONLY these specific well-known names are valid as string names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. Arbitrary folder names (e.g., 'workjournal') are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    },
    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=",
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4="
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the child folder within the parent mail folder from which to retrieve messages. This must be a base64-encoded folder ID (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS. Well-known names are NOT valid for child folders."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing messages from a child folder within a parent mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS
Tool to list subfolders (childFolders) under a specified Outlook mail folder. Use when navigating nested folder hierarchies or checking if a folder has subfolders.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListChildMailFoldersRequest",
  "required": [
    "parent_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of child folders to return. OData $top parameter."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of child folders to skip from the beginning of the result set (OData $skip). Use with $top for pagination."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "isHidden eq false",
        "childFolderCount gt 0"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query to filter the child folders. Example: 'isHidden eq false'."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "displayName",
          "childFolderCount"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of mailFolder properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties include: id, displayName, parentFolderId, childFolderCount, unreadItemCount, totalItemCount, isHidden."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "parent_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parent Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "sentitems",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the parent mail folder. Common well-known names include: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. For folder IDs, obtain them from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or previous childFolders responses. Folder IDs are base64-encoded strings (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') that are mailbox-specific and must come from the same user's mailbox. No URL encoding needed - it's handled automatically."
    },
    "include_hidden_folders": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Hidden Folders",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Include hidden mail folders (isHidden=true) when set to true."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing child folders of a specified mail folder."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CONTACT_FOLDERS_DELTA
Tool to get contact folders that have been added, deleted, or updated. Use when tracking changes to contact folder structure without fetching all folders each time.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListContactFoldersDeltaRequest",
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        "id,displayName",
        "displayName,parentFolderId"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of properties to include in the response. The id property is always returned. Available properties: id, displayName, parentFolderId."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@domain.com"
      ],
      "description": "The ID (user principal name or GUID) of the user. Required for app-only (S2S) authentication. If not provided, uses '/me' endpoint (requires delegated authentication). Accepts both email format (user@domain.com) and GUID format."
    },
    "skiptoken": {
      "type": "string",

## OUTLOOK_LIST_CONTACTS_DELTA
Retrieve incremental changes (delta) of contacts in a specified folder. Use when syncing contacts without fetching the entire set each time. FIRST RUN: Returns ALL contacts in folder. Response has @odata.deltaLink. SUBSEQUENT: Pass stored deltaLink to get only NEW/UPDATED/DELETED contacts since last sync.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListContactsDeltaRequest",
  "required": [
    "contact_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "displayName",
          "emailAddresses"
        ],
        [
          "givenName",
          "surname",
          "companyName",
          "jobTitle"
        ],
        [
          "id",
          "displayName",
          "mobilePhone",
          "businessPhones"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of contact properties to include (e.g. ['displayName','emailAddresses']). Available properties: id, displayName, givenName, surname, middleName, nickName, title, generation, emailAddresses, imAddresses, jobTitle, companyName, department, officeLocation, profession, businessHomePage, assistantName, manager, homePhones, mobilePhone, businessPhones, spouseName, personalNotes, children, homeAddress, businessAddress, otherAddress, categories, birthday, fileAs, initials, yomiGivenName, yomiSurname, yomiCompanyName, parentFolderId, changeKey, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User ID (GUID) or user principal name (email) for app-only (S2S) authentication. Required when using client credentials flow. If not provided, uses '/me' endpoint (delegated auth). Example: '43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f' or 'user@example.com'"
    },
    "skip_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Skip Token",
      "examples": [
        "RPT_CxkRnN...truncated...",
        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/contactFolders/{id}/contacts/delta?$skiptoken=RPT_CxkRnN..."
      ],
      "description": "Skip token for paging through large result sets during initial sync. Accepts either the full @odata.nextLink URL or just the bare token value. Keep paginating until you receive '@odata.deltaLink' instead of nextLink. Mutually exclusive with delta_token - only one should be provided per request."
    },
    "delta_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Delta Token",
      "examples": [
        "h4sICxN9...truncated...",
        "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/contactFolders/{id}/contacts/delta?$deltatoken=h4sICxN9..."
      ],
      "description": "Delta token from a previous call to get only changes since that state. Accepts either the full @odata.deltaLink URL or just the bare token value. If omitted or invalid (placeholders like <token> are ignored), performs initial sync. Response includes @odata.deltaLink - store this for subsequent calls. Mutually exclusive with skip_token - only one should be provided per request."
    },
    "contact_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Contact Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZGwAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "Contact folder identifier (folder GUID). Use GET_CONTACT_FOLDERS action to retrieve available folder IDs."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for retrieving incremental changes (delta) of contacts in a folder."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_EMAIL_RULES
List all email rules from inbox. No server-side filtering is supported; all rule narrowing must be done client-side after retrieval. Each rule includes a `sequence` field defining execution order and may include a `stopProcessingRules` flag affecting downstream rule execution.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListEmailRulesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Number of rules to retrieve. Default is 100. Setting this too low may return an incomplete rule set; use 100 or higher to ensure all rules are retrieved.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Top",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many email rules you want to return in this request. Leave blank to use the default, or enter a number (up to 999) to limit the list."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID or principal name (email) to list email rules for. Required for S2S (app-only) authentication. If not provided, uses the authenticated user context (/me)."
    }
  }
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_EVENTS
Retrieves events from a user's Outlook calendar via Microsoft Graph API. Supports primary/secondary/shared calendars, pagination, filtering, property selection, sorting, and timezone specification. Use calendar_id to access non-primary calendars.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListEventsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of events to retrieve per page for pagination.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Top Events",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many events to return in this batch. Increase to see more results at once."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of initial events to bypass, used for pagination.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Skip Events",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many events to skip from the beginning of the list. Use this to jump ahead when paging through results."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "start/dateTime ge '2024-07-01T00:00:00Z'",
        "start/dateTime ge '2024-07-01T00:00:00Z' and start/dateTime le '2024-07-31T23:59:59Z'",
        "contains(subject, 'Project Review') and categories/any(c:c eq 'Work')"
      ],
      "description": "OData query string to filter calendar events. ONLY the following properties support filtering: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'subject', 'categories', 'importance', 'sensitivity', 'isAllDay', 'isCancelled', 'isReminderOn', 'type'. CRITICAL: Properties like 'body', 'bodyPreview', 'location', 'locations', 'organizer', 'attendees' do NOT support $filter and will cause errors. For text search beyond subject, use the SEARCH_MESSAGES action. IMPORTANT: Use calendar event properties ONLY. Do NOT use mail/message properties like 'receivedDateTime' (which is for emails only). Valid datetime fields for filtering: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime'. For start/end filtering, you MUST use 'start/dateTime' and 'end/dateTime' ONLY. DO NOT use 'start/date' or 'end/date' - these properties do NOT exist on the dateTimeTimeZone type and will cause errors. The 'start/dateTime' and 'end/dateTime' properties work for both all-day events and timed events. Note: 'createdDateTime' and 'lastModifiedDateTime' exist on events but only support $orderby/$select, NOT filtering. DateTime format: \"start/dateTime ge 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'\" (requires single quotes and timezone suffix). Operators: ge (>=), le (<=), eq (=), gt (>), lt (<). DateTime values without quotes or timezone suffix will be automatically normalized.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Filter Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "A simple way to narrow the list, like limiting to a date range or matching a subject. Use it to only return events you care about."
    },

        "type": "string"

          "end",
          "location"
        ],
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "organizer",
          "webLink"
        ],
        [
          "body"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of specific event property names to return. MUST be provided as a list. If omitted, a default set of properties is returned. Valid field names: id, subject, body, bodyPreview, start, end, isAllDay, organizer, attendees, location, locations, recurrence, importance, sensitivity, showAs, categories, hasAttachments, webLink, onlineMeeting, onlineMeetingProvider, onlineMeetingUrl, isOnlineMeeting, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, changeKey, iCalUId, type, seriesMasterId, isOrganizer, isReminderOn, reminderMinutesBeforeStart, responseRequested, responseStatus, allowNewTimeProposals, hideAttendees, isCancelled, isDraft, originalStart, originalStartTimeZone, originalEndTimeZone, transactionId, cancelledOccurrences. Note: 'creator' is NOT a valid field - use 'organizer' instead to get the event creator/organizer. Invalid field names will be automatically filtered out.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Select Properties",
      "human_parameter_description": "Pick which details to include for each event (for example: subject, start, end). This helps keep the response concise and focused."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        [
          "start/dateTime desc"
        ],
        [
          "subject asc",
          "importance desc"
        ],
        [
          "lastModifiedDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of properties to sort results by. Each item is a string like 'start/dateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. MUST be provided as a list, even for single sort criteria. Valid sortable datetime fields: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'createdDateTime', 'lastModifiedDateTime'. Invalid mail properties will be auto-corrected to 'start/dateTime'.",

      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or user identifier of the calendar you want to read. Use 'me' to access your own calendar."

    "timezone": {

Falls back to 'UTC' only if the timezone cannot be resolved.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Timezone",

      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [

        "AAMkADAwATY3ZmYAZS1h"
      ],
      "description": "Optional ID of a specific calendar to retrieve events from. If not provided, uses the default calendar. Get calendar IDs using LIST_CALENDARS action. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use 'primary' or 'default' as values - these are not valid calendar IDs in Microsoft Graph. Leave this field empty/null to access the default calendar. Useful for accessing secondary calendars, shared calendars, or team calendars.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Calendar ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The specific calendar to pull events from. Leave blank for your primary calendar; use this if you want a secondary or shared calendar."

    }
  }

## OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENTS
Tool to get attachments from a message in a specific mail folder. Use when you need to retrieve attachment metadata from a message located in a particular folder.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListMailFolderMessageAttachmentsRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com",
        "me"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID or principal name (email) of the user mailbox to access. Required for app-only (S2S) authentication. Use 'me' or omit for delegated authentication. Example: '43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f' or 'user@domain.com'"
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATM0MDAAMi04OTQ2LTllMjMtMDACLTAwCgBGAAADpmKqHEYNTEGPLqpX05NjpgcAopHWip06p0GbvKmj_O1dLQAAAgEMAAAAopHWip06p0GbvKmj_O1dLQAAAMwwKdcAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the email message from which to retrieve attachments. Must be a message ID obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES or OUTLOOK_SEARCH_EMAILS."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=",
        "sentitems"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the mail folder containing the message. ONLY these specific well-known names are valid as string names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. Arbitrary folder names (e.g., 'workjournal') are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    },
    "include_content": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Content",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Whether to include the base64-encoded file content (contentBytes) in the response. Set to false (default) to return only attachment metadata (id, name, size, contentType, etc.) for efficient listing. Set to true only when you need to download the actual file content."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing attachments from a message in a specific mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGES
Tool to list messages from a specific mail folder including subfolders. Use when you need to retrieve messages from a particular folder or subfolder by its ID or well-known name.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListMailFolderMessagesRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of messages to return per request (1-1000). Always check response['@odata.nextLink'] for pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of messages to skip from the beginning of the result set, for pagination."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "isRead eq false",
        "from/emailAddress/address eq 'sender@example.com'",
        "receivedDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query to filter messages. Examples: 'isRead eq false', 'from/emailAddress/address eq 'sender@example.com'', 'receivedDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'hasAttachments eq true'. Note: Combining complex filters (especially on nested properties like 'from/emailAddress/address') with the 'orderby' parameter may fail with an InefficientFilter error. In such cases, remove 'orderby' or apply sorting client-side."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "from",
          "receivedDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of message properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties include: id, subject, from, toRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, body, bodyPreview, categories, conversationId."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        "receivedDateTime desc",
        "subject asc"
      ],
      "description": "Property to sort results by with direction. OData $orderby parameter. Example: 'receivedDateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. Note: Using 'orderby' together with complex 'filter' queries (especially on nested properties like 'from/emailAddress/address') may fail with an InefficientFilter error. If this occurs, either remove 'orderby' or apply sorting client-side."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=",
        "sentitems"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the mail folder from which to retrieve messages. ONLY these specific well-known names are valid as string names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. Arbitrary folder names (e.g., 'workjournal') are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing messages in a specific mail folder (including subfolders)."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS
Tool to list a user's top-level mail folders. Use when you need folders like Inbox, Drafts, Sent Items; set include_hidden_folders=True to include hidden folders.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListMailFoldersRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of items to return per page.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Page Size",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set the maximum number of mail folders to return in a single request. Useful for controlling response size and implementing pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of items to skip before returning results.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Skip Count",
      "human_parameter_description": "Skip the first N mail folders in the result set. Use with 'top' parameter to implement manual pagination."
    },
    "count": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Count",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Include total count of matching items in the response.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Count",
      "human_parameter_description": "When enabled, the response includes the total count of mail folders in the '@odata.count' property."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "isHidden eq false",
        "totalItemCount gt 0"
      ],
      "description": "OData filter expression to filter mail folders. WARNING: Microsoft Graph API does not officially document which mailFolder properties support filtering. Known unsupported properties: parentFolderId (causes ErrorInvalidProperty error). To filter by parent folder, use the child folders endpoint instead: GET /me/mailFolders/{parentFolderId}/childFolders. Properties like isHidden may work but are not guaranteed.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Filter Expression",
      "human_parameter_description": "Filter mail folders using OData syntax (e.g., 'isHidden eq false'). IMPORTANT: The API does NOT support filtering by 'parentFolderId' - this will cause an error. To get folders under a specific parent, use the 'List Child Mail Folders' action instead with the parent folder ID. Most mailFolder properties are not documented as filterable, so filtering may fail unexpectedly."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        "id,displayName",
        "id,displayName,totalItemCount"
      ],
