## OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS_DELTA
Tool to get incremental changes to mail folders. Use when you need to track additions, deletions, or updates to mail folders without fetching the entire folder list each time.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListMailFoldersDeltaRequest",
  "properties": {
    "select": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        "id,displayName,parentFolderId",
        "displayName,childFolderCount"
      ],
      "description": "OData query parameter to specify only the properties needed for best performance. Comma-separated list of properties (e.g., 'id,displayName,parentFolderId'). The 'id' property is always returned."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com",
        "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-1234-567890abcdef"
      ],
      "description": "Identifier for the user whose mailbox changes to track. Use 'me' for the authenticated user or provide the user's principal name or ID."
    },
    "skiptoken": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Skiptoken",
      "examples": [
        "x9y8z7w6v5u4t3s2r1q0"
      ],
      "description": "A state token returned in the @odata.nextLink URL of the previous delta function call, indicating there are further changes to be tracked in the same round."
    },
    "deltatoken": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Deltatoken",
      "examples": [
        "a0b1c2d3e4f5g6h7i8j9k0"
      ],
      "description": "A state token returned in the @odata.deltaLink URL of the previous delta function call, indicating the completion of that round of change tracking. Include this to get changes since the last complete sync."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for retrieving incremental changes to mail folders."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_ME_EVENT_INSTANCES
DEPRECATED: Use OUTLOOK_LIST_EVENT_INSTANCES instead. Tool to retrieve individual occurrences of a recurring calendar event within a specified time range. Use when you need to get specific instances of a recurring meeting or event series from the authenticated user's primary calendar.

## OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGE_ATTACHMENTS_FROM_CHILD_FOLDER
Tool to list attachments from a message in a nested child mail folder. Use when you need to retrieve attachment metadata from a message located in a subfolder.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListMessageAttachmentsFromChildFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id",
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of attachments to return per request. Check response['@odata.nextLink'] for pagination if more results exist."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "size gt 1000000",
        "isInline eq false"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query to filter attachments. Examples: 'size gt 1000000', 'isInline eq false', 'contentType eq \"application/pdf\"'."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        "id,name,size",
        "id,name,contentType,size"
      ],
      "description": "Comma-separated list of attachment properties to include. Valid properties: id, name, contentType, size, isInline, lastModifiedDateTime. Example: 'id,name,size'."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATM0MDAAMi04OTQ2LTllMjMtMDACLTAwCgBGAAADpmKqHEYNTEGPLqpX05NjpgcAopHWip06p0GbvKmj_O1dLQAAAgEMAAAAopHWip06p0GbvKmj_O1dLQAAAMwwKdcAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the email message from which to retrieve attachments. Must be a message ID obtained from list or search operations, not a folder ID."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the parent mail folder. Valid well-known names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. For custom folders, use the base64-encoded folder ID from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    },
    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExBBB="
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the child folder containing the message. Must be a valid folder ID (base64-encoded string) obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing attachments from a message in a child mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES
Retrieves a list of email messages from a specified mail folder in an Outlook mailbox, with options for filtering (including by conversationId to get all messages in a thread), pagination, and sorting; ensure 'user_id' and 'folder' are valid, and all date/time strings are in ISO 8601 format.

## OUTLOOK_LIST_OUTLOOK_ATTACHMENTS
Lists metadata (name, size, contentType, isInline — but not `contentBytes`) for all attachments of a specified Outlook email message. Returns fileAttachment, itemAttachment, and referenceAttachment types; only fileAttachment entries support download via OUTLOOK_DOWNLOAD_OUTLOOK_ATTACHMENT. Results include inline images and signatures — filter by `isInline == false` and check `contentType` to identify real document attachments. Results are nested under `data.response_data.value`.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListOutlookAttachmentsRequest",
  "required": [
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the user. Use the user's UPN (e.g., 'AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com') or 'me' for the currently authenticated user. This specifies the mailbox to query.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATM0MDAAMi04OTQ2LTllMjMtMDACLTAwCgBGAAADpmKqHEYNTEGPLqpX05NjpgcAopHWip06p0GbvKmj_O1dLQAAAgEMAAAAopHWip06p0GbvKmj_O1dLQAAAMwwKdcAAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the email message from which to retrieve attachments. Must be a message ID (obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES or OUTLOOK_SEARCH_EMAILS), not a folder ID or calendar event ID. Folder IDs look similar but will cause an error. When sourcing from OUTLOOK_SEARCH_EMAILS, use `hitId` as the message identifier \u2014 not `resource.id`.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Message ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of the email message whose attachments you want to list. Get this ID from listing or searching messages - do not use folder IDs."
    }
  }
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_PLACES
Retrieves a collection of place objects defined in a tenant by type. Places can include rooms, workspaces, buildings, floors, sections, desks, and room lists. When room_list_id is provided, returns only rooms or workspaces within that specific room list using the /places/{roomListId}/microsoft.graph.roomlist/rooms (or /workspaces) endpoint. Use this action when you need to discover available physical spaces or locations within an organization. Note: Before using this API, ensure that the Places settings are properly configured in the tenant.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListPlacesRequest",
  "required": [
    "placeType"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 25,
      "maximum": 1000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        25,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of places to return per page. Default is 25. API defaults: 100 for rooms/workspaces/room lists, 1000 for buildings/floors/sections/desks."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        25,
        50
      ],
      "description": "Number of places to skip for pagination (OData $skip)."
    },
    "count": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Count",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Include count of items (OData $count=true). Only supported for room, workspace, and room_list types."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "capacity gt 50",
        "building eq '1'"
      ],
      "description": "OData filter expression to restrict returned places (OData $filter). Only supported for room, workspace, and room_list types. Example: capacity gt 50."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "displayName",
          "emailAddress",
          "capacity"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of place properties to include in the response (OData $select). Example: displayName, emailAddress, capacity."
    },
    "placeType": {
      "enum": [
        "microsoft.graph.room",
        "microsoft.graph.workspace",
        "microsoft.graph.roomlist",
        "microsoft.graph.building",
        "microsoft.graph.floor",
        "microsoft.graph.section",
        "microsoft.graph.desk"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Place Type",
      "examples": [
        "room",
        "building",
        "workspace"
      ],
      "description": "The type of place to retrieve. Choose from: room, workspace, room_list, building, floor, section, or desk."
    },
    "roomListId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Room List Id",
      "examples": [
        "bldg1-rooms@contoso.com"
      ],
      "description": "The email address of a room list. When provided, scopes the results to rooms or workspaces within that specific room list using the MS Graph endpoint GET /places/{roomListId}/microsoft.graph.roomlist/rooms (or /workspaces). Must be the room list's email address (not its ID). Only valid when place_type is 'room' or 'workspace'."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for listing places."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_PRIMARY_CALENDAR_PERMISSIONS
Tool to list calendar permissions from a user's primary calendar. Use when you need to see who has access to the primary calendar and their permission levels.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListPrimaryCalendarPermissionsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        5,
        10
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of permissions to return (OData $top parameter).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Max Permissions",
      "human_parameter_description": "The maximum number of calendar permissions to return. Use this to limit the list if you only need a few results."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        5
      ],
      "description": "Number of permissions to skip (OData $skip parameter).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Skip Count",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many calendar permissions to skip from the start of the list. Use this to move to the next page of results."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User ID or userPrincipalName. Use 'me' for the signed-in user.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose calendar permissions you want to list. Use 'me' to list permissions for your own primary calendar."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request to list calendar permissions."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_REMINDERS
Tool to retrieve reminders for events occurring within a specified time range. Use when you need to see upcoming reminders between two datetimes.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListRemindersRequest",
  "required": [
    "startDateTime",
    "endDateTime"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "userId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@contoso.onmicrosoft.com"
      ],
      "description": "User Principal Name or ID. Use 'me' to indicate the signed-in user.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose reminders you want to see. Enter 'me' to use your own account."
    },
    "endDateTime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "End Date Time",
      "examples": [
        "2023-10-26T20:00:00.0000000",
        "2024-01-01T23:59:59.0000000"
      ],
      "description": "The end date and time in ISO 8601 format defining the window for reminders. Example: '2023-10-26T20:00:00.0000000'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "End DateTime",
      "human_parameter_description": "The latest date and time to look for reminders. Set when the time window should end so results stop at this point."
    },
    "startDateTime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Start Date Time",
      "examples": [
        "2023-10-26T19:00:00.0000000",
        "2024-01-01T00:00:00.0000000"
      ],
      "description": "The start date and time in ISO 8601 format defining the window for reminders. Example: '2023-10-26T19:00:00.0000000'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Start DateTime",
      "human_parameter_description": "The earliest date and time to look for reminders. Set when the time window should start so you only see reminders from this point onward."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for retrieving event reminders within a time window."
}

## OUTLOOK_LIST_SENT_ITEMS_MESSAGES
Tool to list all messages in the SentItems mail folder of the signed-in user's mailbox. Use when you need to retrieve sent messages with optional filtering and sorting.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListSentItemsMessagesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of messages to return per request (1-1000). Always check response['@odata.nextLink'] for pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of messages to skip from the beginning of the result set, for pagination."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "isRead eq false",
        "sentDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "hasAttachments eq true"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query to filter messages. Examples: 'isRead eq false', 'toRecipients/any(a:a/emailAddress/address eq \"recipient@example.com\")', 'sentDateTime ge 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z', 'hasAttachments eq true'. Note: Combining complex filters with the 'orderby' parameter may fail with an InefficientFilter error. In such cases, remove 'orderby' or apply sorting client-side."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "toRecipients",
          "sentDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of message properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties include: id, subject, from, toRecipients, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, body, bodyPreview, categories, conversationId."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        "sentDateTime desc",
        "subject asc"
      ],
      "description": "Property to sort results by with direction. OData $orderby parameter. Example: 'sentDateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. Note: Using 'orderby' together with complex 'filter' queries may fail with an InefficientFilter error. If this occurs, either remove 'orderby' or apply sorting client-side."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User ID (GUID) or user principal name (email) of the user whose sent items to list. Required for app-only (S2S) authentication. Not required for delegated authentication (uses signed-in user by default)."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing messages in the SentItems mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_USER_CALENDAR_EVENT_INSTANCES
Tool to retrieve instances (occurrences) of a recurring event from a specific calendar within a date range. Use when you need event instances from a particular calendar.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUserCalendarEventInstancesRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "calendar_id",
    "event_id",
    "startDateTime",
    "endDateTime"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        25,
        50
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of event instances to return per page (OData $top). Controls page size for pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of event instances to skip from the beginning of the result set (OData $skip). Use with $top for pagination."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "testcompud@outlook.com",
        "48d31887-5fad-4d73-a9f5-3c356e68a038"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the user (can be user ID, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for authenticated user)."
    },
    "event_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Event Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQ0AAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mNLwAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the recurring event (seriesMaster) for which to retrieve instances."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHO0AAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar containing the event."
    },
    "endDateTime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "End Date Time",
      "examples": [
        "2026-04-30T23:59:59.0000000",
        "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
      ],
      "description": "The end date and time of the time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2026-04-30T23:59:59.0000000'). Only instances that start within or overlap this range will be returned."
    },
    "startDateTime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Start Date Time",
      "examples": [
        "2026-03-01T00:00:00.0000000",
        "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "description": "The start date and time of the time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2026-03-01T00:00:00.0000000'). Only instances that start within or overlap this range will be returned."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for listing instances of a recurring event from a specific calendar."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_USER_CALENDAR_GROUPS_CALENDAR_VIEW
Tool to get calendar view from a specific calendar within a calendar group for a user. Use when retrieving events from a calendar that belongs to a calendar group.

**Input schema:**
```json

  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUserCalendarGroupsCalendarViewRequest",

    "user_id",

    "calendar_id",
    "startDateTime",
    "endDateTime"

## OUTLOOK_LIST_USER_CALENDARS_EVENTS
Tool to retrieve events from a specific calendar for a user. Use when you need to list calendar events for a specific user by user ID and calendar ID.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUserCalendarsEventsRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "calendar_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 10,
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of events to retrieve per page for pagination."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of initial events to bypass, used for pagination."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "start/dateTime ge '2024-07-01T00:00:00Z'",
        "start/dateTime ge '2024-07-01T00:00:00Z' and start/dateTime le '2024-07-31T23:59:59Z'",
        "contains(subject, 'Project Review') and categories/any(c:c eq 'Work')"
      ],
      "description": "OData query string to filter calendar events. ONLY the following properties support filtering: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'subject', 'categories', 'importance', 'sensitivity', 'isAllDay', 'isCancelled', 'isReminderOn', 'type'. CRITICAL: Properties like 'body', 'bodyPreview', 'location', 'locations', 'organizer', 'attendees' do NOT support $filter and will cause errors. IMPORTANT: Use calendar event properties ONLY. Do NOT use mail/message properties like 'receivedDateTime'. For start/end filtering, you MUST use 'start/dateTime' and 'end/dateTime' ONLY. DO NOT use 'start/date' or 'end/date' - these properties do NOT exist and will cause errors. DateTime format: \"start/dateTime ge 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'\" (requires single quotes and timezone suffix). Operators: ge (>=), le (<=), eq (=), gt (>), lt (<). DateTime values without quotes or timezone suffix will be automatically normalized."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "subject",
          "start",
          "end",
          "location"
        ],
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "organizer",
          "webLink"
        ],
        [
          "body"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of specific event property names to return. MUST be provided as a list. If omitted, a default set of properties is returned. Valid field names: id, subject, body, bodyPreview, start, end, isAllDay, organizer, attendees, location, locations, recurrence, importance, sensitivity, showAs, categories, hasAttachments, webLink, onlineMeeting, onlineMeetingProvider, onlineMeetingUrl, isOnlineMeeting, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, changeKey, iCalUId, type, seriesMasterId, isOrganizer, isReminderOn, reminderMinutesBeforeStart, responseRequested, responseStatus, allowNewTimeProposals, hideAttendees, isCancelled, isDraft, originalStart, originalStartTimeZone, originalEndTimeZone, transactionId, cancelledOccurrences. Note: 'creator' is NOT a valid field - use 'organizer' instead. Invalid field names will be automatically filtered out."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        [
          "start/dateTime desc"
        ],
        [
          "subject asc",
          "importance desc"
        ],
        [
          "lastModifiedDateTime"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of properties to sort results by. Each item is a string like 'start/dateTime desc' or 'subject asc'. MUST be provided as a list, even for single sort criteria. Use 'asc' (default) or 'desc' for order. IMPORTANT: Use calendar event properties ONLY. Do NOT use mail/message properties like 'receivedDateTime'. Valid sortable datetime fields: 'start/dateTime', 'end/dateTime', 'createdDateTime', 'lastModifiedDateTime'."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "user@example.com",
        "AdeleV@contoso.onmicrosoft.com",
        "6640adbb5cb743b0"
      ],
      "description": "The user's primary SMTP address, user principal name (UPN), or user ID to identify the calendar owner."
    },
    "timezone": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Timezone",
      "default": "UTC",
      "examples": [
        "America/New_York",
        "Eastern Standard Time",
        "UTC",
        "Europe/London"
      ],
      "description": "Preferred timezone for event start/end times. Accepts IANA format (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Tokyo') or Windows format (e.g., 'Eastern Standard Time', 'Pacific Standard Time'). Falls back to 'UTC' if the timezone cannot be resolved."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHO0AAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar to retrieve events from."
    }
  }
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_USER_CALENDAR_VIEW
Tool to get calendar view from a specific user's calendar. Use when you need to retrieve events that occur or overlap with a specified time window from a user's specific calendar by calendar ID.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUserCalendarViewRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "calendar_id",
    "startDateTime",
    "endDateTime"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 20,
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        20,
        50
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of events to retrieve."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "subject",
          "start",
          "end",
          "location"
        ],
        [
          "id",
          "subject",
          "organizer",
          "isAllDay"
        ],
        [
          "subject",
          "start",
          "end",
          "body"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of event properties to return. Defaults to commonly-needed fields excluding the full HTML body. To include the full body content, explicitly add 'body' to this list."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "john.doe@example.com",
        "48d31887-5fad-4d73-a9f5-3c356e68a038"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the user or 'me' for the authenticated user. This can be the user's email address or their unique identifier."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAEYAAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKBwDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQYAAADGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACHO0AAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar to retrieve events from. Get calendar IDs using the LIST_CALENDARS action."
    },
    "endDateTime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "End Date Time",
      "examples": [
        "2024-12-31T23:59:59-08:00",
        "2024-10-04T00:00:00+00:00",
        "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
      ],
      "description": "The end date and time of the time range in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59-08:00' or '2024-12-31T23:59:59+00:00' for UTC). Events active up to this time will be included."
    },
    "startDateTime": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Start Date Time",
      "examples": [
        "2024-01-01T00:00:00-08:00",
        "2024-10-03T00:00:00+00:00",
        "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      ],
      "description": "The start date and time of the time range in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (e.g., '2024-01-01T00:00:00-08:00' or '2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00' for UTC). Events active during this window will be returned."
    }
  }
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_USER_CONTACTS
Tool to retrieve contacts from a specific user's mailbox. Use when you need to list or browse contacts for a given user.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUserContactsRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of contacts to return. OData $top parameter."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "Number of contacts to skip for pagination. OData $skip parameter."
    },
    "count": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Count",
      "description": "If true, includes a count of the total number of items in the result. OData $count parameter."
    },
    "expand": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Expand",
      "examples": [
        [
          "extensions"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Related entities to expand inline. OData $expand parameter."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "emailAddresses/any(a:a/address eq 'garth@contoso.com')",
        "startswith(displayName,'A')"
      ],
      "description": "OData filter expression to filter contacts. Example: emailAddresses/any(a:a/address eq 'garth@contoso.com') or startswith(displayName,'A')."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "id",
          "displayName",
          "emailAddresses"
        ],
        [
          "givenName",
          "surname"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of properties to include in the response. OData $select parameter. Valid properties: displayName, givenName, surname, emailAddresses, mobilePhone, businessPhones, jobTitle, companyName, etc."
    },
    "orderby": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Orderby",
      "examples": [
        [
          "displayName asc"
        ],
        [
          "surname desc",
          "givenName asc"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of properties to order results by. OData $orderby parameter. Format: 'property asc' or 'property desc'."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com",
        "6640adbb5cb743b0"
      ],
      "description": "User principal name or ID of the user. Use 'me' for the authenticated user."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for retrieving contacts for a specific user."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_LIST_USERS
Tool to list users in Microsoft Entra ID. Use when you need to retrieve a paginated list of users, optionally filtering or selecting specific properties. For single-user lookups, prefer a dedicated get-user tool — listing all users is significantly heavier and slower.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListUsersRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "maximum": 999,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        50,
        100
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of users to return (OData $top). Default page size is 100, maximum is 999.",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many users to return in this call. Choose a number to control page size; higher numbers return more users at once."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        50
      ],
      "description": "Number of users to skip (OData $skip) for pagination.",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many users to skip before starting to return results. Use this to continue where the last page left off."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "startswith(displayName,'J')",
        "accountEnabled eq true"
      ],
      "description": "OData filter expression to restrict returned users (OData $filter). For targeted lookups, use `userPrincipalName eq 'user@domain.com'` or `mail eq 'user@domain.com'` to avoid full-list pagination scans.",
      "human_parameter_description": "A simple filter to narrow the list of users you get back, like names that start with 'J' or only enabled accounts."
    },
    "select": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Select",
      "examples": [
        [
          "displayName",
          "mail",
          "userPrincipalName"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of user properties to include in the response (OData $select).",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose which user fields you want included in the results, such as display name, email, or user principal name."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for listing users in Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)."
}
```

  "title": "ListUsersResponseWrapper",
  "required": [
    "data",
    "successful"

                "title": "State",
                "description": "State or province. Max 128 characters."
              },

                "type": "string",
                "title": "My Site",
                "description": "URL for the user's personal site."
              },

                "type": "array",

                },

                "type": "string",
                "title": "Birthday",

              },
              "jobTitle": {
                "type": "string",

## OUTLOOK_MOVE_MAIL_FOLDER
Tool to move a mail folder and its contents to another mail folder. Use when you need to reorganize the folder hierarchy.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "MoveMailFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "folder_id",
    "destination_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's email address, UPN, or 'me' for the currently authenticated user.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox."
    },
    "folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "Unique ID of the mail folder to move. Must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Folder ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of the mail folder you want to move. You can get this from a previous folder list operation."
    },
    "destination_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Destination Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "deleteditems",
        "AAMkADhAAAAAAEKAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The destination folder ID, or a well-known folder name (e.g., 'inbox', 'deleteditems', 'drafts', 'sentitems'). The folder being moved will become a child of this destination folder. If using a folder ID, it must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Destination ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Where you want to move the folder to. The folder will become a child folder of this destination. You can use folder names like 'inbox' or 'deleteditems', or provide a specific folder ID."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for moving a mail folder and its contents to another mail folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_MOVE_MESSAGE
Move a message to another folder within the specified user's mailbox. Creates a new copy in the destination folder and removes the original. The message_id changes after a successful move; use the ID returned in the response for any subsequent operations on the moved message. High-volume parallel moves can trigger HTTP 429 (MailboxConcurrency) throttling; honor the Retry-After header.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "MoveMessageRequest",
  "required": [
    "message_id",
    "destination_id"
  ],

    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",

      "default": "me",

        "me",

      ],

      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",

    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "Unique ID of the Outlook email message to move. Must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Message ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of the email message you want to move. You can get this from a previous message search or list operation."
    },
    "destination_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Destination Id",
      "examples": [
        "deleteditems",
        "inbox",
        "AAMkADhAAAAAAEKAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The destination folder ID, or a well-known folder name (e.g., 'inbox', 'deleteditems', 'drafts', 'sentitems'). If using a folder ID, it must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs. Prefer folder IDs over well-known names \u2014 some tenants reject well-known names like 'deleteditems'. Retrieve current folder IDs via OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS rather than hard-coding, as IDs can become stale. Display names are localized and non-unique; never use display names as the destination_id.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Destination ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Where you want to move the message. You can use folder names like 'inbox' or 'deleteditems', or provide a specific folder ID."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for moving a message to another folder."
}

## OUTLOOK_MOVE_MESSAGE_FROM_CHILD_FOLDER
Tool to move a message from a child folder to another destination folder. Use when you need to move a message that exists within a specific folder hierarchy (parent folder → child folder → message).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "MoveMessageFromChildFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "user_id",
    "mail_folder_id",
    "child_folder_id",
    "message_id",
    "destinationId"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "6640adbb5cb743b0",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's id, userPrincipalName, or user object ID."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "Unique ID of the Outlook email message to move. Must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs."
    },
    "destinationId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Destination Id",
      "examples": [
        "deleteditems",
        "inbox",
        "AAMkADhAAAAAAEKAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The destination folder ID, or a well-known folder name (e.g., 'inbox', 'deleteditems', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'junkemail'). If using a folder ID, it must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAACAQ8AAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the parent mail folder. Common well-known names include: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. For folder IDs, obtain them from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS. Folder IDs are base64-encoded strings (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=')."
    },
    "child_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Child Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "AQMkADAwATMwMAExLTlmNjktOWVmYS0wMAItMDAKAC4AAAPLkCuWz0mbS4RvWyTvc1LKAQDGTYrvat2PSKIu8IS9hMqyAAAAU0mZPAAAAA=="
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the child folder containing the message. Obtain this from OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS. Child folder IDs are base64-encoded strings (e.g., 'AAMkADAwATMwMAExAAA=')."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for moving a message from a child folder to another folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_MOVE_MESSAGE_FROM_FOLDER
Tool to move a message from a specific mail folder to another destination folder. Use when you need to move a message and know both the source folder ID and the message ID.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "MoveMessageFromFolderRequest",
  "required": [
    "mail_folder_id",
    "message_id",
    "destinationId"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "User's email address, UPN, or 'me' for the currently authenticated user."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "Unique ID of the Outlook email message to move. Must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs."
    },
    "destinationId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Destination Id",
      "examples": [
        "deleteditems",
        "inbox",
        "drafts",
        "AAMkADhAAAAAAEKAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The destination folder ID, or a well-known folder name (e.g., 'inbox', 'deleteditems', 'drafts', 'sentitems'). If using a folder ID, it must be the complete, untruncated ID string - do not use shortened or ellipsis-containing IDs."
    },
    "mail_folder_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mail Folder Id",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=",
        "sentitems"
      ],
      "description": "The ID or well-known name of the mail folder containing the message. ONLY these specific well-known names are valid as string names: 'inbox', 'drafts', 'sentitems', 'deleteditems', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'outbox', 'clutter', 'conflicts', 'conversationhistory', 'localfailures', 'msgfolderroot', 'recoverableitemsdeletions', 'scheduled', 'searchfolders', 'serverfailures', 'syncissues'. Arbitrary folder names are NOT valid. If the folder is not one of these well-known names, you MUST use the actual folder ID - a base64-encoded string (e.g., 'AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA=') obtained from OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS or OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request parameters for moving a message from a specific mail folder to another folder."
}
```

## OUTLOOK_PERMANENT_DELETE_MESSAGE
Permanently deletes an Outlook message by moving it to the Purges folder in the dumpster. Unlike standard DELETE, this action makes the message unrecoverable by the user. IMPORTANT: This is NOT the same as DELETE - permanentDelete is irreversible and availability differs by national cloud deployments (not available in US Government L4, L5 (DOD), or China (21Vianet)).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PermanentDeleteMessageRequest",
  "required": [

## OUTLOOK_PIN_MESSAGE
Tool to pin a message in an Outlook chat. Use when you want to mark an important message for quick access.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "PinMessageRequest",
  "required": [
    "chat_id",
    "message_url"
  ],

      "type": "string",
      "title": "Chat Id",
      "examples": [

      ],
      "description": "ID of the chat where the message will be pinned."

      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",

        "user@example.com"

      "title": "Message Url",

    }
  },
  "description": "Request schema for pinning a chat message in Outlook."
}

## OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS
Query Outlook emails within a SINGLE folder using OData filters. Build precise server-side filters for dates, read status, importance, subjects, attachments, and conversations. Best for structured queries on message metadata within a specific folder. Returns up to 100 messages per request with pagination support. • Searches SINGLE folder only (inbox, sentitems, etc.) - NOT across all folders • For cross-folder/mailbox-wide search: Use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES • Server-side filters: dates, importance, isRead, hasAttachments, subjects, conversationId • CRITICAL: Always check response['@odata.nextLink'] for pagination • Limitations: Recipient/body filtering requires OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "QueryEmailsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "top": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Top",
      "default": 100,
      "maximum": 1000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        10,
        50,
        100,
        500
      ],
      "description": "Maximum number of messages to return per request (1-1000). Default is 100. IMPORTANT: For large mailboxes, always check response['@odata.nextLink'] to fetch remaining messages. Pagination example: 1) Call with top=100, 2) Check if '@odata.nextLink' exists in response, 3) If present, make a new request to that full URL (includes $skiptoken), 4) Repeat until '@odata.nextLink' is absent.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Max Results",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many messages to return in this request. Use a smaller number for faster responses; you can page for more if needed."
    },
    "skip": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Skip",
      "default": 0,
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        100,
        200
      ],
      "description": "Number of messages to skip for pagination. NOTE: For large result sets, prefer using '@odata.nextLink' from responses instead of manual skip.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Skip",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many messages to skip from the start, useful for paging through results. Usually you can leave this at 0 and follow the next page link instead."
    },
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Filter",
      "examples": [
        "isRead eq false",
        "importance eq 'high'",
        "hasAttachments eq true",
        "receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z",
        "receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z and receivedDateTime lt 2025-10-08T00:00:00Z",
        "isRead eq false and receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z",
        "importance eq 'high' and hasAttachments eq true",
        "startswith(subject, '[Task Update]')",
        "startswith(subject, 'Re:') and hasAttachments eq true",
        "subject eq 'Weekly Report'",
        "conversationId eq 'AQQkADAwATY3ZmYAZS1hYQAzNC1lODkwLTAwAi0wMAoAEADJzjh8m93SQbP6BUCZcIuc'",
        "sentDateTime gt 2025-10-01T14:30:00Z and sentDateTime lt 2025-10-01T18:00:00Z",
        "isDraft eq false and isRead eq false and importance eq 'high'",
        "(isRead eq false or importance eq 'high') and receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z",
        "(isRead eq false or importance eq 'high') and hasAttachments eq true",
        "from/emailAddress/address eq 'user@example.com'",
        "startswith(from/emailAddress/address, 'support@')",
        "from/emailAddress/address eq 'boss@company.com' and isRead eq false",
        "categories/any(a:a eq 'Priority')",
        "categories/any(a:a eq 'Priority') or categories/any(b:b eq 'Urgent')",
        "categories/any(a:a eq 'Priority') and isRead eq false"
      ],
      "description": "OData $filter query string to filter email messages. Syntax: 'field operator value' combined with 'and', 'or', 'not'.\n\n        **IMPORTANT - DO NOT include 'folder' in this filter:**\n        - The 'folder' field is NOT a valid filter property for messages\n        - To specify which folder to query, use the separate 'folder' parameter (e.g., folder=\"inbox\")\n        - WRONG: filter=\"folder eq 'inbox' and isRead eq false\"\n        - CORRECT: folder=\"inbox\", filter=\"isRead eq false\"\n\n        **Operators:** eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge, startswith(), contains(), any()\n\n        **String Functions (Auto-Corrected):**\n        - CORRECT: `contains(subject, 'text')`, `startswith(subject, 'prefix')`\n        - If you use invalid syntax like `subject_contains 'text'`, it will be auto-corrected to `contains(subject, 'text')`\n        - Supported functions for subject: contains(), startswith()\n        - Supported functions for from/sender: startswith() only (exact match with eq also works)\n        - NOTE: endswith() is NOT reliably supported by Microsoft Graph API for message filtering\n\n        **Common Fields (Server-Side Filterable):**\n        - `isRead` - Boolean: true/false\n        - `importance` - String: 'low', 'normal', 'high'\n        - `subject` - String (exact match or startswith)\n        - `hasAttachments` - Boolean: true/false\n        - `receivedDateTime`, `sentDateTime` - DateTime (ISO 8601: '2025-10-01T00:00:00Z')\n        - `conversationId` - String (exact match)\n        - `categories` - Array (use any() operator - see Categories Filtering below)\n        - `isDraft`, `isRead`, `flag/flagStatus` - Boolean/String flags\n\n        **NOT FILTERABLE - id and messageType fields:**\n        - `id` - Message ID is NOT filterable with $filter. To retrieve a specific message by ID, use OUTLOOK_GET_MESSAGE instead\n        - `messageType` - This property does NOT exist on Message resources (only on EventMessage resources). Cannot be used in filters\n\n        **Categories Filtering (IMPORTANT SYNTAX):**\n        - Single category: `categories/any(a:a eq 'CategoryName')`\n        - Multiple categories (OR): Use SEPARATE any() calls combined with 'or':\n          `categories/any(a:a eq 'Cat1') or categories/any(b:b eq 'Cat2')`\n        - NOTE: `categories/any(c: c eq 'Cat1' or c eq 'Cat2')` (OR inside any()) returns 400 errors\n        - Category names must be quoted with single quotes and match exactly\n\n        **Sender Filtering (SUPPORTED):**\n        - `from/emailAddress/address` - Filter by sender email: `from/emailAddress/address eq 'user@example.com'`\n        - `sender/emailAddress/address` - Filter by sender: `sender/emailAddress/address eq 'user@example.com'`\n        - Use startswith() for partial matches: `startswith(from/emailAddress/address, 'user@')`\n        - IMPORTANT: ONLY the 'address' field is filterable. The 'name' field (display name) is NOT filterable with OData $filter\n        - WRONG: `from/emailAddress/name eq 'Ellen van Huisseling'` (name field is not filterable)\n        - CORRECT: `from/emailAddress/address eq 'user@example.com'` (address field is filterable)\n        - NOTE: contains() is NOT supported on sender/from fields. For partial sender name matching (e.g., finding emails from senders containing 'motion'), use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES with KQL syntax like `from:motion`\n\n        **NOT FILTERABLE - Use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES instead:**\n        - `toRecipients`, `ccRecipients`, `bccRecipients` - Recipient filtering requires KQL search\n        - Common mistake: `to`, `cc`, `bcc` are NOT valid property names (correct names are `toRecipients`, `ccRecipients`, `bccRecipients`)\n        - `body/content` - Body text search requires KQL search\n\n        **Date Filtering:**\n        - Dates MUST be in ISO 8601 format with time zone: 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z\n        - IMPORTANT: DateTimeOffset values are NOT enclosed in quotes (Microsoft Graph requirement)\n        - Use ge (>=), gt (>), le (<=), lt (<) operators\n        - Example: `receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z and receivedDateTime lt 2025-10-02T00:00:00Z`\n        - The validator will automatically remove quotes if you accidentally include them\n        - Do NOT include sort keywords (asc/desc) in the filter - use the separate 'orderby' parameter instead\n\n        **String Filtering:**\n        - Exact match: `subject eq 'Meeting Notes'`\n        - Starts with: `startswith(subject, '[Action Required]')`\n        - Escape single quotes by doubling: `subject eq 'Owner''s Manual'`\n\n        **Combining Conditions:**\n        - AND: `isRead eq false and importance eq 'high'`\n        - OR: `importance eq 'high' or importance eq 'low'`\n        - NOT: `not (isRead eq true)`\n        - Grouping: `(isRead eq false or importance eq 'high') and hasAttachments eq true`\n",
      "human_parameter_name": "Filter Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Use a simple expression to narrow results by things like unread status, dates, subject, or attachments. For example: isRead eq false or receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z. Note: Datetime values should NOT have quotes around them."
    },
    "folder": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Folder",
      "default": "inbox",
      "examples": [
        "inbox",
        "sentitems",
        "drafts",
        "AAMkAGI0ZjExAAA="

Well-known names (case-insensitive): 'inbox', 'sentitems', 'drafts', 'deleteditems', 'outbox', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'clutter', 'recoverableitemsdeletions'. For custom folders (e.g., 'Billing', 'Projects'), you MUST provide the folder ID (a long base64-like string like 'AAMkAGU0NTRiNDA4...'). Use OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS to get folder IDs for custom folders. Do NOT pass folder URLs or display names. IMPORTANT: To search across ALL folders, use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES instead (searches entire mailbox without folder restriction). NOTE: This parameter also accepts 'folder_id' as an alias for backwards compatibility.",

## OUTLOOK_REPLY_EMAIL
Sends a plain text reply to an Outlook email message, identified by `message_id`, allowing optional CC and BCC recipients.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ReplyToEmailRequest",
  "required": [
    "message_id",
    "comment"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "comment": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Comment",
      "examples": [
        "Thank you for your email. I'll review and respond shortly."
      ],
      "maxLength": 10000,
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The plain text body of the reply email.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Comment",
      "human_parameter_description": "What you want to say in your reply. Enter the plain text message that will be sent to the original sender and recipients."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "user@example.com",
        "me"
      ],
      "description": "The user's email address or 'me' to indicate the authenticated user. This specifies the mailbox from which the reply will be sent.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address of the mailbox you want to reply from. Use 'me' to send the reply from your own account."
    },
    "cc_emails": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Cc Emails",
      "default": [],
      "examples": [
        [
          "jane.doe@example.com",
          "other@example.com"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of email addresses for CC recipients.",
      "human_parameter_name": "CC Emails",
      "human_parameter_description": "People you want to keep in the loop on this reply. Add one or more email addresses to CC them."
    },
    "bcc_emails": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Bcc Emails",
      "default": [],
      "examples": [
        [
          "manager@example.com",
          "supervisor@example.com"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of email addresses for BCC recipients.",
      "human_parameter_name": "BCC Emails",
      "human_parameter_description": "People you want to include privately on this reply. Add email addresses to BCC so other recipients won't see them."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The Microsoft Graph message ID (NOT an email address). This is a Base64-encoded string typically starting with 'AAMk' (e.g., 'AAMkAGI2TAAA='). Do NOT pass email addresses like 'user@example.com'. Obtain this ID from the 'id' field returned by `OUTLOOK_LIST_MESSAGES`, `OUTLOOK_GET_MESSAGE`, or `OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES` actions.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Message ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of the email you want to reply to (NOT an email address). This is a long encoded string like 'AAMkAGI2TAAA=' from the 'id' field in message lists. Do not use the 'conversationId' field or email addresses."
    }
  }
}
```

## OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES
Search Outlook messages using powerful KQL syntax. Supports sender (from:), recipient (to:, cc:), subject, date filters (received:, sent:), attachments, and boolean logic. Only works with Microsoft 365/Enterprise accounts (no @hotmail.com/@outlook.com). Examples: 'from:user@example.com AND received>=2025-10-01', 'to:info@jcdn.nl AND subject:invoice', 'received>today-30 AND hasattachment:yes'

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SearchMessagesRequest",
  "properties": {
    "size": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Size",
      "default": 25,
      "maximum": 25,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Number of search results to return per page (1-25). Note: For message entity, max size is 25. Also, from_index + size cannot exceed 1000 (API pagination window limit).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Page Size",
      "human_parameter_description": "How many results to return per page. Use a larger number to see more results at once."
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "default": "",
      "examples": [
        "project report",
        "from:manager@example.com AND subject:budget",
        "to:info@jcdn.nl AND (subject:toegangscontrole OR subject:beveiligingspoorten)",
        "received>=2025-10-01 AND received<=2025-10-31",
        "received>today-30 AND hasattachment:yes",
        "from:example.com AND subject:invoice AND received:2025-10",
        "to:team@example.com AND received>=2025-10-01",
        "cc:manager@example.com OR to:manager@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "KQL (Keyword Query Language) search query string. Supports advanced syntax for precise searches.\n\n**Basic Syntax:**\n- Simple keywords: 'budget report'\n- Exact phrases: '\"quarterly review\"'\n- Boolean operators: 'urgent AND deadline' or 'invoice OR receipt'\n\n**Property Filters (prefix:value):**\n- from: Sender email - 'from:user@example.com' or 'from:example.com'\n- to: Recipient email - 'to:info@jcdn.nl'\n- cc: CC recipient - 'cc:manager@example.com'\n- subject: Subject line - 'subject:invoice'\n- received: Date received - 'received:2025-10-01' or 'received>=2025-10-01'\n- sent: Date sent - 'sent:2025-10-01' or 'sent>=2025-10-01'\n- hasattachment: Has files - 'hasattachment:yes' or 'hasattachment:no'\n\n**Date Operators:**\n- Exact: 'received:2025-10-01'\n- Greater/equal: 'received>=2025-10-01'\n- Less/equal: 'received<=2025-10-31'\n- Range: 'received:2025-10-01..2025-10-31'\n- Relative: 'received>today-7' (last 7 days)\n\n**Combining Filters:**\n- AND: 'from:user@example.com AND subject:invoice'\n- OR: 'to:sales@example.com OR to:support@example.com'\n- Complex: 'from:example.com AND (subject:urgent OR subject:important) AND received>=2025-10-01'\n\n**REQUIRED**: At least one search criterion must be provided - either this query parameter OR one of the legacy filters (fromEmail, subject, hasAttachments). Empty searches are not supported.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "What you want to search for in your mailbox. You can type simple words or use filters like from:, to:, subject:, received:, and hasattachment: to narrow the results."
    },
    "region": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Region",
      "examples": [
        "US",
        "EU",
        "GB"
      ],
      "description": "Geographic region for the search query. ONLY required when using application permissions (S2S authentication). ## OUTLOOK_SEND_DRAFT
Tool to send an existing draft message. Use after creating a draft when you want to deliver it to recipients immediately. Example: Send a draft message with ID 'AAMkAG…'.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SendDraftRequest",
  "required": [
    "message_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user's email address or 'me' to represent the authenticated user.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the mailbox you want to send from. Use 'me' to send from your own account."
    },
    "message_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Message Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGVi..."
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the draft message to send.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Draft Message ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique ID of the draft email you want to send. You can get this from the draft you just created or from a previous list or search."
    }
  }
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {
    "SendDraftResponse": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "SendDraftResponse",
      "properties": {},
      "description": "Response for sending a draft message. The API returns 202 Accepted with an empty body.\nThis model represents the successful acceptance of the send request."
    }
  },
  "title": "SendDraftResponseWrapper",
  "required": [
    "data",
    "successful"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "Data",
      "properties": {},
      "description": "Data from the action execution"
    },
    "error": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Error",
      "description": "Error if any occurred during the execution of the action"
    },
    "successful": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Successful",
      "description": "Whether or not the action execution was successful or not"
    }
  }
}
```

## OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL
Sends an email with subject, body, recipients, and an optional attachment via Microsoft Graph API. Supports comma-separated email addresses in the to_email field for multiple recipients. Attachments require a non-empty file with valid name and mimetype.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SendEmailRequest",
  "required": [
    "subject",
    "body",
    "to"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "to": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "To",
      "examples": [
        "recipient@example.com",
        "john.doe@company.com",
        "alice@example.com, bob@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The primary recipient's email address(es). You can provide a single email or multiple emails separated by commas. Valid email addresses will be extracted from strings containing extra text. Format: name@domain.com",
      "human_parameter_name": "Recipient Email(s)",
      "human_parameter_description": "Who you want to send the email to. Enter one address or multiple separated by commas."
    },
    "body": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Body",
      "examples": [
        "Hello team, please find the attached report.",
        "<h1>Project Phoenix</h1><p>Initial proposal attached.</p>"
      ],
      "description": "The content of the email body as a plain string (plain text or HTML based on `is_html`). Do not pass structured objects; provide only the raw text/HTML content.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Email Body",
      "human_parameter_description": "What you want to say in the email. Enter plain text or include HTML if you turn on HTML format."
    },
    "is_html": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Is Html",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        "true",
        "false"
      ],
      "description": "Specifies if the email body is HTML; `True` for HTML, `False` for plain text.",
      "human_parameter_name": "HTML Format",
      "human_parameter_description": "Turn this on if your message includes HTML formatting (headings, links, bold). Leave off for plain text."
    },
    "subject": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subject",
      "examples": [
        "Project Update",
        "Important Announcement"
      ],
      "maxLength": 255,
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "The subject line of the email.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Email Subject",
      "human_parameter_description": "What you want the email to be titled so recipients know what it's about."
    },
    "to_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "To Name",
      "examples": [
        "Valued Customer",
        "John Doe"
      ],
      "description": "The display name of the primary recipient.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Recipient Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "The display name for the main recipient so their name appears alongside their email address."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "specific.user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user's email address or the alias 'me' to represent the authenticated user.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or ID of the mailbox to send from. Use 'me' to send from your own account."
    },

## OUTLOOK_UPDATE_CALENDAR_EVENT
Updates specified fields of an existing Outlook calendar event. Implementation note: To avoid unintentionally clearing properties, the action first fetches the existing event, merges only the provided fields, and then PATCHes the merged updates. Unspecified fields remain unchanged.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpdateEventRequest",
  "required": [
    "event_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "body": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "BodyContent",
      "required": [
        "contentType",
        "content"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "content": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Content",
          "examples": [
            "Let's meet to discuss the updated project details."
          ],
          "description": "The actual content of the event body, corresponding to the specified contentType."
        },
        "contentType": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Content Type",
          "examples": [

          ],
          "description": "The format of the event body. Must be 'Text' for plain text or 'HTML' for HTML content."
        }
      },
      "description": "Event body with content type ('Text' or 'HTML') and the content. If omitted, the existing body remains unchanged.",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "human_parameter_name": "Event Body",
      "human_parameter_description": "Details or agenda for the event. Provide only if you want to modify the current body."
    },
    "show_as": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Show As",
      "examples": [
        "busy"
      ],
      "description": "Availability status for the event. Valid values: 'free', 'tentative', 'busy', 'oof'. If omitted, the existing status remains unchanged.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Show As",
      "human_parameter_description": "How your availability appears during the event (free, tentative, busy, out of office). Omit to keep current setting."
    },
    "subject": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subject",
      "examples": [
        "Updated Team Meeting"
      ],
      "description": "New subject for the event. If provided as an empty string, the subject will be cleared. If omitted, the existing subject remains unchanged.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Event Subject",
      "human_parameter_description": "The title you want to show on the calendar for this event. Provide an empty string to clear it; omit to keep the current subject."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "description": "The identifier of the user whose calendar event is to be updated. Accepts the user's principal name, ID, or 'me' for the currently authenticated user.",
      "human_parameter_name": "User ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The email address or identifier of the user whose calendar you want to update. Use 'me' to update your own calendar."
    },
    "event_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Event Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],

      "human_parameter_name": "Event ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique ID of the calendar event you want to update. You can get this from a previous event search or list."
    },
    "location": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": true
        }
      ],
      "title": "Location",
      "examples": [
        "Conference Room A",
        "{\"displayName\": \"Conference Room A\"}"
      ],
      "description": "Event location. Can be provided as a simple string (e.g., 'Conference Room A') which will be converted to displayName, or as a dictionary with fields like displayName, address, etc. If provided, replaces the existing primary location. Omit to leave unchanged.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Event Location",
      "human_parameter_description": "Where the event takes place. Provide a simple name like 'Noida' or an object with displayName and other details. Omit to keep current location."
    },
    "attendees": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",

## OUTLOOK_UPDATE_CALENDAR_EVENT_IN_CALENDAR
Tool to update an event in a specific Outlook calendar. Use when you need to modify event details like subject, time, attendees, or location in a non-default calendar.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpdateCalendarEventInCalendarRequest",
  "required": [
    "calendar_id",
    "event_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "body": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "BodyContent",
      "required": [
        "contentType",
        "content"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "content": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Content",
          "examples": [
            "Let's meet to discuss the updated project details."
          ],
          "description": "The actual content of the event body, corresponding to the specified contentType."
        },
        "contentType": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Content Type",
          "examples": [
            "HTML"
          ],
          "description": "The format of the event body. Must be 'Text' for plain text or 'HTML' for HTML content."
        }
      },
      "description": "Event body with content type ('Text' or 'HTML') and the content. If omitted, the existing body remains unchanged.",
      "additionalProperties": false
    },
    "show_as": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Show As",
      "examples": [
        "busy"
      ],
      "description": "Availability status for the event. Valid values: 'free', 'tentative', 'busy', 'oof'. If omitted, the existing status remains unchanged."
    },
    "subject": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subject",
      "examples": [
        "Updated Team Meeting"
      ],
      "description": "New subject for the event. If provided as an empty string, the subject will be cleared. If omitted, the existing subject remains unchanged."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user ID or principal name (email) of the user whose calendar event to update. Required for app-only (S2S) authentication. If not provided, uses the authenticated user context (/me endpoint) for delegated authentication."
    },
    "event_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Event Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar event to be updated. This ID can be obtained from the OUTLOOK_LIST_EVENTS action."
    },
    "location": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": true
        }
      ],
      "title": "Location",
      "examples": [
        "Conference Room A",
        "{\"displayName\": \"Conference Room A\"}"
      ],
      "description": "Event location. Can be provided as a simple string (e.g., 'Conference Room A') which will be converted to displayName, or as a dictionary with fields like displayName, address, etc. If provided, replaces the existing primary location. Omit to leave unchanged."
    },
    "attendees": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "Attendee",
        "required": [
          "emailAddress",
          "type"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "type": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Type",
            "examples": [
              "required"
            ],
            "description": "The attendee's type. Valid values are 'required' or 'optional'."
          },
          "emailAddress": {
            "type": "object",
            "title": "Email Address",
            "required": [
              "address"
            ],
            "properties": {
              "name": {
                "type": "string",
                "title": "Name",
                "default": "",
                "examples": [
                  "Jane Doe"
                ],
                "description": "The display name of the attendee."
              },
              "address": {
                "type": "string",
                "title": "Address",
                "examples": [
                  "jane.doe@example.com"
                ],
                "description": "The complete email address of the attendee."
              }
            },
            "description": "The email address and optional name of the attendee.",
            "additionalProperties": false
          }
        }
      },
      "title": "Attendees",
      "description": "Attendee list for the event. If provided, replaces the existing attendees. If omitted, attendees remain unchanged."
    },
    "time_zone": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Time Zone",
      "examples": [
        "America/Los_Angeles"
      ],
      "description": "Time zone for the provided start_datetime and/or end_datetime (IANA or Windows time zone names). If omitted, the existing event's time zone is used."
    },
    "categories": {
      "type": "array",

## OUTLOOK_UPDATE_CALENDAR_GROUP
Tool to update the properties of a calendar group object. Use when you need to rename a calendar group.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpdateCalendarGroupRequest",
  "required": [
    "calendar_group_id",
    "name"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Name",
      "examples": [
        "Updated Test Calendar Group",
        "Work Calendars"
      ],
      "description": "The new name for the calendar group."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "default": "me",
      "examples": [
        "me",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The user's principal name (UPN) or object ID. Use 'me' for the authenticated user."
    },
    "calendar_group_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Calendar Group Id",
      "examples": [
        "AAMkAGI2TAAA="
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar group to update. This ID can be obtained from the list calendar groups action."
    }
  }
}
```

        },

      }
    }
  },
  "title": "UpdateCalendarGroupResponseWrapper",

    "data",
    "successful"
  ],

      "type": "object",
      "title": "Data",

      ],
      "properties": {

          "title": "Id",
          "description": "The unique identifier of the calendar group. Read-only."
        },
        "name": {
          "type": "string",

## OUTLOOK_UPDATE_CALENDAR_GROUP_CALENDAR_PERMISSION
Tool to update a calendar permission within a calendar group. Use when changing access levels for calendars in specific groups.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpdateCalendarGroupCalendarPermissionRequest",
  "required": [
    "calendar_group_id",
    "calendar_id",
    "permission_id",
    "role"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "role": {
      "enum": [
        "freeBusyRead",
        "limitedRead",
        "read",
        "write"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Role",
      "examples": [
        "read",
        "write"
      ],
      "description": "The permission level to change to for the calendar share recipient. Options: freeBusyRead (view availability only), limitedRead (view availability and titles), read (view all event details), write (view and edit events)."
    },
    "user_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User Id",
      "examples": [
        "43f0c14d-bca8-421f-b762-c3d8dd75be1f",
        "user@example.com"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier or email address of the user. Required for S2S (app-only) authentication. If not provided, defaults to 'me' for delegated authentication."
    },
    "calendar_id": {
      "type": "string",
